questions.question: Why does a recommendation about routine population skin-cancer screening not resolve the care of a changing mole?
choices: A changing lesion is a patient-specific diagnostic problem that needs clinical evaluation
Population recommendations prohibit lesion examination
Changing lesions are always benign
Only dermatologists may ask about evolution
questions.explanation: Population screening guidance and evaluation of a new, changing, bleeding, or nonhealing lesion are different questions. A concerning lesion needs an individualized diagnostic plan.

questions.question: Which history most strongly increases concern for a lesion needing timely diagnostic evaluation?
choices: A stable lesion unchanged for decades
A lesion that is new or evolving, bleeds spontaneously, or repeatedly fails to heal
A lesion that becomes less noticeable with time
A lesion located under clothing
questions.explanation: Evolution, new growth, recurrent bleeding, and nonhealing behavior are important warning features. Location under clothing does not make a lesion safe.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate use of the ABCDE framework for a pigmented lesion?
choices: It is a prompt for careful assessment, not a rule that proves or excludes melanoma
It diagnoses melanoma when any one feature is present
It is only useful in light skin tones
It replaces documenting the lesion size and history
questions.explanation: Asymmetry, border, color, diameter or darkening, and evolution help structure assessment. Melanoma can be atypical, and clinical context, objective description, and diagnostic evaluation remain necessary.

questions.question: Which action is safest when a lesion has meaningful concern for melanoma?
choices: Destroy it empirically with cryotherapy before a diagnostic plan
Arrange biopsy-capable or dermatology evaluation rather than repeated empirical treatment
Tell the patient to photograph it only if it becomes painful
Treat with a topical antibiotic for several months
questions.explanation: Destructive therapy can delay or complicate diagnosis of a suspicious lesion. A timely biopsy or specialist pathway is safer when melanoma is a meaningful consideration.

questions.question: A patient with dark skin presents with a new widening pigmented streak in a nail. What is the best FNP approach?
choices: Dismiss it because melanoma only occurs on sun-exposed light skin
Recognize nail-unit change can be concerning and arrange timely specialist evaluation
Reassure if there is no pain
Treat the nail with an over-the-counter antifungal without examination
questions.explanation: Skin cancer can occur across skin tones and in nail or acral locations. New or changing nail pigmentation deserves careful assessment and appropriate referral.

questions.question: Which documentation practice most supports safe suspicious-lesion follow-up?
choices: Record only the word mole
Document change history, objective size and morphology, site, differential, urgency, and referral plan
Avoid noting uncertainty
Wait for the patient to remember the prior size
questions.explanation: Objective documentation, including the clinical question and expected follow-up, supports comparison, referral quality, and closed-loop tracking.

questions.question: Which finding is most compatible with a possible basal cell carcinoma pattern?
choices: A repeatedly bleeding or nonhealing pearly, translucent, ulcerated papule or plaque
A transient symmetric rash after exercise
A stable freckle unchanged since childhood
A deep muscle contusion after trauma
questions.explanation: Basal cell carcinoma may present as a persistent pearly, translucent, ulcerated, or bleeding lesion, though appearances vary. Persistent nonhealing behavior requires assessment.

questions.question: What is the primary FNP role after placing a referral for a suspicious lesion?
choices: Assume the referral is complete once it is entered
Track appointment completion and pathology or specialist recommendations
Delete the concern from the problem list
Wait until the next annual visit regardless of urgency
questions.explanation: Closed-loop care means confirming that the patient accessed evaluation and that pathology or specialist recommendations are reviewed and incorporated into the plan.

questions.question: Which prevention message is most accurate?
choices: Sunscreen means a changing lesion can be observed indefinitely
Ultraviolet protection and avoiding tanning reduce risk but do not replace evaluation of a concerning lesion
Only people with light skin need ultraviolet protection
A prior sunburn makes diagnostic evaluation unnecessary
questions.explanation: Sun protection is useful prevention, but it does not rule out skin cancer or replace timely evaluation of a suspicious lesion.

questions.question: Which patient most clearly needs expedited assessment?
choices: A stable symmetric benign-appearing lesion with no change
A persistent crusted ear lesion that repeatedly bleeds in an immunocompromised patient
A freckle that fades in winter
A healed abrasion from yesterday
questions.explanation: Persistent bleeding, nonhealing lesions and immunocompromise increase concern and justify an expedited biopsy or dermatology pathway.
